newsitem.title: USA: NGC reports sharply higher profits.
newsitem.headline: NGC reports sharply higher profits.

text.p: NGC Corp. reported sharply higher fourth-quarter profits Thursday, attributing the rise to its acquisition of Chevron Corp.'s natural gas unit and improved results from its gas processing, natural gas liquids and crude oil businesses.

The Houston-based energy company reported net income of $47.7 million, or 28 cents a share, for the quarter, a 165 percent increase from the $18 million, or 15 cents per share, it earned in the fourth quarter of 1995.
The results topped the average Wall Street analyst forecast of 26 cents per share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst predictions.
NGC, which has operations in North America and Britain, posted revenues of $2.95 billion, up 173 percent from the $1.08 billion in the year-ago quarter.
"NGC completed the most exciting and profitable year in its history," company Chairman Chuck Watson said in a statement.
Watson said the strong results reflected the first full quarter of benefits from the acquisition of Chevron's natural gas unit, which closed Aug. 31.
The company also credited the strong numbers to substantially improved results from gas processing, natural gas liquids sales and crude oil sales.
NGC stock rose 12.5 cents to $21.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
